entries.title: Opening Summary starts writing it if needed
entries.body: Pressing Summary on the mode bar, or choosing 'Generate the main modes' when you add an article, starts writing the summary in plain words straight away, rather than waiting for you to press 'Write it'. While it is being written, the panel no longer says nobody has asked for it.

entries.title: Archive an article from the top of it
entries.body: If an article is yours, an Archive button sits at the top of the page, beside the button for sharing it publicly, and turns into Put back once the article is archived. You can file a piece away without leaving it.

entries.title: The mode panel widens on wide windows
entries.body: On a wide window, the panel beside the article, where modes such as Summary and Glossary appear, takes some of the empty space the article's text cannot use, up to a limit. Less of the screen sits empty.

entries.title: Gift emails recognise readers who have accounts
entries.body: A gift voucher sent to the address of a confirmed Spideryarn account arrives as a gift, not an invitation to sign up. On Free, the email says how many articles you have left before and after, counting other gifts waiting; on a paid plan, that it counts once you are on Free. The privacy page says so.

entries.title: Articles no longer scroll sideways slightly
entries.body: On a computer set to always show scrollbars, such as a Mac with that setting, every article could be scrolled sideways a little, because the page was laid out as if the scrollbar took no room. The article fits the window again.

entries.title: Metadata page shows its contents on iPads
entries.body: An article's Metadata page hid its list of contents on mid-sized screens, including an iPad held sideways, even with room to spare. The list appears there too, and the page's main text moves over just enough to make room for it.
